concerns.text: Tasks T010 (Sanitize), T012 (Deduplicate), T013 (Sample), and T014 (Descriptors) are marked as [X] (completed) but depend on T009 (Download ChEMBL) which is marked as [ ] (pending/rejected). The 'Producer before Consumer' rule is violated: the data pipeline tasks claim to process data that has not yet been produced by the download task.

Task T015 (Write Processed Data) requires validating against `contracts/molecule.schema.yaml`, but T004 (Setup Contracts) is marked as [ ] (pending). A consumer task (validation) cannot proceed before its producer (schema definition) is complete.

Tasks T018 (Train Linear Regression) and T019 (Train Random Forest) are marked as [ ] (pending/rejected) but are prerequisites for T022-T026 (Evaluation). The task list implies a linear progression where evaluation tasks are ready, yet the model artifacts they consume do not exist. This breaks the data-flow dependency chain.

Task T034 (Run full pipeline verification) is a mandatory gate that depends on the entire pipeline (Download -> Process -> Train -> Evaluate) being functional. Since T009 (Download) and T018/T019 (Training) are blocked/rejected, T034 cannot be executed. Listing it as a pending task in a broken state violates the 'Foundational tasks first' principle.

T001 (Create project structure) and T003 (Configure linting) are marked [ ] (pending) but are foundational prerequisites for all subsequent code implementation tasks (T005-T038). While T005-T007 are marked [X], the lack of project structure (T001) and linting config (T003) creates a semantic dependency violation for the tasks marked as complete.
